summary: AI observability has become essential in 2026 as LLM-powered applications scale, giving teams visibility into prompts, traces, output quality, hallucinations, and token costs. Without observability, teams risk runaway API spend, undetected quality regressions, and compliance gaps. The market now spans lightweight cost-tracking proxies to full evaluation and tracing platforms with self-hosted and enterprise options.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end LLM traces, prompts, chains/agents, token usage, latency, and evaluation metrics—especially for LangChain-based applications.
features: Deep trace and span visualization for chains and agents
tools.pricing: Developer tier free up to 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month; overage around $2.50 per 1,000 traces at standard retention (roughly £80/month at 100K traces). Enterprise custom.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on LangChain that need rich debugging and evaluation workflows.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API requests and costs as a lightweight gateway/proxy, tracking spend across 300+ models, latency, and usage per user or department.
features: Cost computation across 300+ models via model-cost repository
tools.pricing: Free up to 10,000 requests/month; Growth/Pro at $20/month for 100K requests (reported ~$79 USD at the 100K-trace milestone on some plans). Enterprise custom.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting the simplest, cheapest setup for instant cost governance and spend tracking.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: ML/LLM experiments, model training runs, prompt and LLM traces (via W&B Weave), evaluations, and system metrics.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals/personal use; team and enterprise plans are seat-based with custom/usage pricing for larger teams.
tools.best_for: ML teams that want unified experiment tracking plus LLM observability in one platform.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: Production LLM and ML model performance, drift, embeddings, traces, hallucinations, and evaluation metrics.
features: Arize Phoenix open-source tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Phoenix is free and open-source; Arize cloud/enterprise offers managed tiers with custom usage-based pricing.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing production-grade ML and LLM monitoring with drift detection and evals.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompts, token/cost usage, evaluations, and quality alerting, with a strong open-source self-hosted option.
features: Cost and token tracking per trace
tools.pricing: LangFuse Cloud free for under 50K requests, then ~£20-£30/month at higher volumes; self-hosted ~£30/month infra plus ~2hrs/month maintenance.
tools.best_for: Self-hosted teams wanting an open-source, cost-effective trace store with evals and alerting.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, token usage, and latency via OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation, exportable to any compatible backend.
features: Vendor-neutral export to existing observability backends
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; cost depends on the OpenTelemetry backend you export to (e.g., Datadog, Grafana, Traceloop).
tools.best_for: Teams wanting standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation that plugs into existing observability stacks.

cost_tips: Route requests through a cost-tracking gateway or proxy (like Helicone) to get per-user and per-model spend visibility and catch runaway usage early.
Use smaller or cheaper models for simple tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning, cascading only when needed.
Cache frequent or identical responses and reuse embeddings to avoid paying repeatedly for the same computations.
Trim prompts and context windows—remove redundant tokens, compress history, and set max-token limits to reduce input/output costs.
Set usage alerts and budget thresholds with anomaly detection so cost spikes are flagged before they become expensive surprises.
